back: From dzimba dza mabwe: houses of stone.

front: When was Great Zimbabwe at its height (approx.)?

back: Goods or labour given to a ruler by subject chiefs and people as a sign of loyalty.
Building walls of shaped stone blocks without mortar.
Spirits of royal ancestors (lion spirits) who guard the land, speaking through mediums.

front: Founder of the Mutapa state in tradition?
back: Nyatsimba Mutota; his son Matope expanded it.

front: Exports and imports of Great Zimbabwe?
back: Exports: gold and ivory. Imports: glass beads, cloth, Chinese and Persian pottery.

front: Name three theories for the decline of Great Zimbabwe.
back: Exhaustion of resources; shift in the gold trade to the north; drought; succession disputes.

front: Why did the Mutapa state decline?
back: Civil wars over succession, Portuguese interference, breakaway provinces and the rise of the Rozvi.
